The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(2x-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{(2x-1)^{2}-1}}\cdot (2x-1)^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{(4{x}^{2}-4x+1)-1}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}-4x}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{4x(x-1)}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{x(x-1)}}.\end{aligned}
$$
